parsed.explanation: Combined regime imposes birth-sex access in government bathrooms, locker rooms, dormitories, shelters and prisons, with no statewide service protection and a religious-refusal immunity allowing denial of service. Federal entry practice creates document-discrepancy refusal and a possible permanent fraud finding, and federal custody documents hormone removal, forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse. Litigation, existing X passports until expiry, 15 protective cities, and no documented state presentation sweeps or arrest under its own facilities law limit severity, but universal facility/custody exposure has no documented working remedy. That is below a single-domain bathroom ban and above organised targeting.

entry_documents.exposure: Foreign passports accepted, but X markers no longer issued; discrepancy/doubt on sex instructs refusal and possible permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation. Reports of confiscated/blocked passports and stranded travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and limited waivers exist. Passport policy is in litigation.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from entry refusal to investigation/fraud allegation, then detention and birth-sex placement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: State law includes prisons; national immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men. Federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy model: short hair, hormone removal.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented visitor-specific custody placement protection or remedy. Some national orders are blocked/enjoined, but custody policies described remain operative in dossier.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for facilities trespass, entry fraud investigation, or immigration detention leads into birth-sex incentive custody and care denial.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: March 2025 state law defines woman/man as binary sex and covers bathrooms, locker rooms, rape-crisis centres, dormitories and prisons. Federal order bars government-funded facilities congruent with identity.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 15 cities bar gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations; private hotels may differ. No state-wide protection; 2023 religious-refusal law permits denial with qualified immunity.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State and federal bans overlap in government buildings; city protections cannot override state/federal facility, prison or shelter rules.

care_services.exposure: Emergency/hospital ward placement under birth-sex rule is not separately documented for this state, but facilities law reaches shelters/crisis centres. Adult insurance coverage ruling was overturned in 2026, pending challenge unresolved. Hormone removal in custody documented.
care_services.protection: Adult care challenge pending; no documented operative visitor care shield. Litigation has blocked some national orders, outcome uncertain.
care_services.interaction: Emergency admission or custody can trigger birth-sex placement and interruption of prescribed hormone care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official framing treats gender diversity as threat: governor says spaces kept private for women only; federal counterterrorism prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups and reward/investigation directives on gender ideology in schools.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No presentation offence or police sweeps documented for this state; targeting is via facilities, documents and custody rules. Courts have enjoined several federal orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing supports enforcement of facility/document rules and makes complaints/investigations riskier than ordinary service disputes.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans puberty blockers/hormones/surgery for minors except severe dysphoria by two physicians; schools facilities are covered by bans; April 2025 bill would require outing trans students to parents, final status unresolved. Federal directive seeks prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. Protective city ordinances do not override state minor-care or school facility rules.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor faces school/public facility exclusion and potential outing; a guardian may face investigation or care-access barriers if seeking care in state.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented pattern of street violence against visitors, police sweeps, or rate of bias assaults in this state. National hate-crime law covers gender identity, but only 23 states have state bias statutes per dossier.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute and courts provide some recourse; no state-wide anti-discrimination statute, religious-refusal immunity weakens service recourse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response is documented only through facilities arrest example in another state and custody abuse nationally; visitor assault reporting outcomes not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No documented arrest/prosecution under this state's March 2025 law, no documented refusal to a trans visitor under religious-refusal law, and final status of outing and ordinance-nullification bills unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation and city ordinances are partial remedies, but no documented remedy successfully displacing state/federal facility or custody rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns do not neutralise known universal exposures; enforcement frequency is uncertain while possibility is carried by every outed visitor.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: birth-sex public facilities with document checking and complaints routinely failing. This case is broader (shelters, dormitories, prisons, entry fraud risk, custody hormone removal) but has more litigation, city protections and no documented ward-assault pattern, so slightly above 0.35.

Lower than 0.45-A: that anchor is bathrooms only, emergency care ordinary, no organised arrests, one prosecution. Here exposure spans entry, prisons/shelters/dormitories, service-refusal immunity, federal custody abuse and state threat framing, so materially below 0.45.

Much lower than 0.65-A: that anchor has lawful presentation, identity facilities, corrected hotel refusals and convicted attackers. Here facility/custody rules are unremedied, entry can trigger refusal/fraud consequences, and service denial is legally immunised in circumstances.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one interacting system: a foreign passport discrepancy can lead to refusal or a fraud investigation; any detention leads to birth-sex prison placement and documented hormone/care denial; ordinary movement leads to birth-sex government facilities including shelters and dormitories; and service refusals may be immunised. City ordinances and pending litigation mitigate private settings but do not displace state/federal facility, entry or custody rules. No sweeps, presentation criminalisation or documented visitor violence pattern keeps it above 0.25-0.35, while multi-domain universal exposure without working remedy keeps it in elevated risk around 0.40.
